vue-fundamentals-sr8-07.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation presented nested writes to an object prop as a sanctioned capability and left out the docs' advice against them. The statement and answer are unchanged. (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr8-07.statement: A child's nested writes to an object prop change the shared object held in the parent's state.
vue-fundamentals-sr8-07.explanation: Objects are passed by reference, so Vue blocks only reassigning the prop itself. The docs advise avoiding such writes unless parent and child are tightly coupled, and emitting an event instead.

vue-fundamentals-sr9-12.reason: ambiguous: the docs call useAttrs() non-reactive, but the Vue 3.5 runtime tracks reads through the attrs proxy and triggers on changes, so the old card could be refuted by experiment. I replace it with the verifier's suggested section fact (attribute casing in $attrs), confirmed on the attrs page: 'Unlike props, fallthrough attributes preserve their original casing in JavaScript, so an attribute like foo-bar needs to be accessed as $attrs['foo-bar']'. I removed the verifier's onClick clause from the explanation because it is the answer to sr9-11. New factKey: attrs-original-casing. (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr9-12.statement: In `$attrs`, Vue stores a parent's fallthrough `foo-bar` attribute under the camelCase key `fooBar`.
vue-fundamentals-sr9-12.explanation: Unlike props, fallthrough attributes keep their original casing in JavaScript, so a child reads a foo-bar attribute as `$attrs['foo-bar']`.
vue-fundamentals-sr9-12.misconception: Fallthrough attribute names are camelCased in $attrs the way prop names are.

vue-fundamentals-sr12-08.reason: ambiguous: 'first calls onActivated when ... returns from the cache' can be read as 'the first hook on re-insertion'. The new wording states only the false claim, that the hook waits for a cache re-insertion, and avoids the compound form the verifier suggested ('runs on X but skips Y'). Confirmed in the page's code comment: 'called on initial mount and every time it is re-inserted from the cache'. (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr12-08.statement: Vue delays a kept-alive component's onActivated hook until the component is re-inserted from the cache.
vue-fundamentals-sr12-08.explanation: onActivated runs on a kept-alive component's initial mount and again every time the component is re-inserted from the cache.
vue-fundamentals-sr12-08.misconception: Activation callbacks begin only with the first restoration from the cache.

vue-fundamentals-sr14-02.reason: ambiguous: the hedge 'can keep a ref as private state' is defensible in a client-only app. The new wording tests what Pinia treats as state. Confirmed: 'you must return all state properties in setup stores for Pinia to pick them up as state ... Not returning all state properties or making them readonly will break SSR, devtools, and other plugins.' (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr14-02.statement: In Pinia, a ref that a Setup Store leaves out of its returned object still becomes part of the store's state.
vue-fundamentals-sr14-02.explanation: Pinia picks up state only from the properties a Setup Store returns, so the docs say to return every state property; leaving one out breaks SSR, devtools and plugins.
vue-fundamentals-sr14-02.misconception: Every ref declared inside a Setup Store becomes store state, even when it is not returned.

vue-fundamentals-sr8-04.reason: tell: 'by default' marked false (8 false vs 2 true). This rewording removes it and keeps the fact (props are optional unless required: true) and the answer (false). Confirmed: 'All props are optional by default, unless required: true is specified.' (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr8-04.statement: In a runtime declaration, `defineProps({ title: String })` makes title a required prop.
vue-fundamentals-sr8-04.explanation: String only declares the value type; runtime-declared props stay optional unless their declaration specifies required: true.
vue-fundamentals-sr8-04.misconception: A constructor declaration makes the prop required.

vue-fundamentals-sr3-09.reason: tell: adds 'by default' to a true card, which pushes that tell toward balance (now 5 false vs 3 true). The fact (the default in-place patch strategy) and the answer (true) are unchanged. The source moves to the guide that states it with these words: 'by default it uses an in-place patch strategy ... instead of moving the DOM elements to match the order of the items, Vue will patch each element in-place'. (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr3-09.statement: By default, Vue patches v-for list elements in place instead of moving them when the data order changes.
vue-fundamentals-sr3-09.explanation: Without keys, Vue keeps each DOM element at its index and updates its content: efficient, but unsafe when items hold child component state or form input values.

vue-fundamentals-sr11-11.reason: tell: 'returns' marked false (9 false vs 1 true). This rewording drops it and keeps the fact (CSS Modules class names are hashed) and the answer (false). Confirmed: 'The resulting classes are hashed to avoid collision'. (final: fixed)
vue-fundamentals-sr11-11.statement: For a class panel declared in `<style module>`, `$style.panel` holds the unchanged class name panel.
vue-fundamentals-sr11-11.explanation: Vue hashes CSS Modules classes to avoid collisions, so $style.panel holds the generated class name rather than panel, which scopes the class to the current component.
vue-fundamentals-sr11-11.misconception: CSS Modules keep the source class name in $style.

vue-fundamentals-sr7-08.reason: tell: the SSR prefix predicted the answer ('In a server-rendered app' 3 true / 0 false, 'During SSR' 1 true / 3 false). This card moves to the other prefix (now 2T/1F and 1T/2F) and drops 'returns'. The fact (renderToString returns a Promise) and the answer (false) are unchanged. Confirmed: the signature is 'Promise<string>'. (final: keep)
vue-fundamentals-sr7-08.statement: In a server-rendered app, renderToString() produces the rendered HTML synchronously as a plain string.
vue-fundamentals-sr7-08.explanation: renderToString() from vue/server-renderer gives a Promise that resolves to the rendered HTML, so server code awaits it.
vue-fundamentals-sr7-08.misconception: Server HTML rendering hands back its final string synchronously.

vue-fundamentals-sr3-10.reason: tell: the false template 'Vue puts X on the FIRST child/root/named slot' carried three cards (sr3-10, sr9-10, sr10-03), over the limit of two. This rewording removes 'first' and keeps the fact (the key of a template v-for goes on the template tag) and the answer (false). The source moves to the current guide: 'When using <template v-for>, the key should be placed on the <template> container'. (final: fixed)
vue-fundamentals-sr3-10.statement: In a `<template v-for>`, the key attribute belongs on the child elements inside the template.
vue-fundamentals-sr3-10.explanation: Vue expects the key of a <template v-for> on the <template> tag itself, because the template is the unit that repeats for each item.
vue-fundamentals-sr3-10.misconception: Template loop keys belong on the children, as in Vue 2.
